mechanism_chain: A one-day rainfall trigger produced a 68.2 mm gridded peak and at least 39.0 mm at the drier point sample.
The triggering rain arrived 21 days after the Thomas Fire, with mean dNBR about 2.95 times the annual surface-change mean.
Debris flows traveled at least 3.0 km along five main runout paths across alluvial fans.
The exposed AOI contains about 120050 people, 52 critical facilities, and 947 mapped road ways, so response load extends beyond the hillslope source area.

primary_gt.final_interpretation: The package supports a very high post-fire debris-flow coupling: intense one-day rainfall arrived only 21 days after the Thomas Fire, burn-scar metrics are much stronger than annual background surface change, and multi-kilometer runout crossed populated alluvial-fan corridors with dense road and critical-facility exposure.

criteria.name: Self-directed package discovery and citations
criteria.description: Finds relevant event report, precipitation, burn-scar, annual-change, population, and map-exposure records, and cites package-relative paths for values used.
criteria.partial_credit: Award up to 2 points for incomplete but plausible source discovery; no full credit without package-relative citations.

criteria.name: Event and report anchor extraction
criteria.description: Extracts the one-day event window, 21-day burn lag, 1140 km2 fire area, at least 3 km runout, five runout paths, 23 fatalities, and at least 400 damaged homes.
criteria.partial_credit: Award proportional credit for correct report values and unit conversions.

criteria.name: Rainfall trigger calculations
criteria.description: Computes the gridded peak rainfall, same-source mean ratio, largest spatial concentration ratio, point rainfall floor/ceiling, grid-to-point ratio, and rainfall-trigger normalization.
criteria.partial_credit: Award partial credit for correct formulas with minor source-selection or rounding mistakes.

criteria.name: Burn-scar conditioning calculations
criteria.description: Uses dNBR and annual embedding-change statistics to compute burn-severity ratios and the burn-conditioning normalization.
criteria.partial_credit: Award partial credit for correct extraction but incomplete normalization.

criteria.name: Exposure and impact synthesis
criteria.description: Counts population, critical facilities, road ways, and impact rates, then derives runout-exposure and impact normalizations.
criteria.partial_credit: Award proportional credit for correct counts and rates.

criteria.name: Process and scenario model
criteria.description: Applies the specified weighted formulas, reports the baseline process index and response score, recomputes the wetter/higher-exposure scenario, and gives deltas and label shift.
criteria.partial_credit: Award partial credit for correct baseline or scenario calculations when the other is incomplete.

criteria.name: Structured scientific interpretation
criteria.description: Provides valid JSON and a concise mechanism-based interpretation tied to rainfall, burn conditioning, runout, and exposure.
criteria.partial_credit: Award this point only when the interpretation is grounded in computed package evidence.

provenance.notes: Ground truth is derived from local package report text plus precipitation, dNBR, annual surface-change, population, and OSM-style exposure records.
